facts.value: An application is possible without a completed Bachelor’s degree if at least 80% of the required credits in the Bachelor’s program have been completed by the time of application.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: If you have not completed your Bachelor’s degree, please apply with the following additional application documents by May 15: proof of enrollment in the Bachelor’s program and a preliminary transcript of records that includes an average grade and all previous exam results.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: The preliminary transcript must be issued by an authorized institution for grading.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: The 80% criterion is binding, and unfortunately, exceptions are not possible.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: For a maximum of 180 ECTS Bachelor’s degree, a minimum of 144 ECTS is required for application.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: For a maximum of 210 ECTS Bachelor’s degree, a minimum of 168 ECTS is required for application.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: For a maximum of 240 ECTS Bachelor’s degree, a minimum of 192 ECTS is required for application.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: In the absence of a Bachelor’s certificate, only provisional admission can initially be granted, subject to successful completion of the Bachelor’s degree.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: The Bachelor’s degree certificate must be submitted by the end of the first semester of the Master’s program to obtain final admission.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: It is strongly recommended to complete all necessary Bachelor’s coursework in the summer semester prior to the Master's program to ensure a successful start.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: If your degree was obtained at a university outside Germany, an online application via the Uni Assist portal is sufficient.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: For application to a higher semester, a request for credit recognition and a performance overview of completed courses must be submitted.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: The request and performance overview must be submitted by the application deadline (January 15 or May 15).
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: Credits not yet recorded can be recognized if a request for recognition is submitted with the application.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: The program is restricted in all semesters.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: For the summer semester, applications can be made for the second or fourth semester by January 15 or May 15.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: For the winter semester, applications can be made for the third semester.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: Enrollment in a higher semester can only occur if open study places are available and the corresponding ECTS credits to be recognized are present.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: For up to 30 ECTS, students are classified into the 2nd semester.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: For 31 to 60 ECTS, students are classified into the 3rd semester.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: For 61 to 90 ECTS, students are classified into the 4th semester.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: If open study places are available and more applications for the higher semester are received, a ranking is created according to the valid selection regulations.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: Example applications for recognition: Summer semester application with 3 courses of 6 ECTS each, relevant ECTS: 18, classification: 2nd semester.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: Example applications for recognition: Summer semester application with 9 courses of 6 ECTS each, relevant ECTS: 54, classification: No classification possible, as the relevant ECTS only allow classification into the 3rd semester, which is not possible in the summer semester.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: Example applications for recognition: Summer semester application with 5 courses of 6 ECTS each, relevant ECTS: 30, classification: 2nd semester.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance

facts.value: Example applications for recognition: Winter semester application with 11 courses of 6 ECTS each, relevant ECTS: 66, classification: Classification not possible.
facts.programme_association: Master in Money, Macro and Finance
